q1_issues.issue: The explicit adversative connective "but" joining the two reified eventualities gets no surface-headed connective atom (`(But sk_lose_1 sk_stop_1)`), which Inter-clause connectives requires for an adversative.

"lost to Vinnie Rossano" is a non-spatial, non-transfer "to"-phrase that answers neither "whither" nor "to whom", so by the "decide by the question the PP answers, never by which listed role is closest" rule it should be the preposition-named oblique rather than `Goal`.
"stopped Joey DeJohn" has an object that is not created, destroyed, consumed or physically changed, so the unclear-case default `Theme` applies rather than `Patient`.

q2_gaps: completive/frame "in N <unit>" adverbial ("in five rounds"): the Time section supplies a duration form only for "for N <time-unit>" / "lasted N", and "round" is not a unit the measure/conversion lexicon covers, so the extent of a bout has no specified encoding

adversative "but" coordinating two VPs under one elided subject: Coordination & plurals says translate each conjunct independently while Inter-clause connectives defines "but" over two clauses, and neither section says which governs VP-level coordination
notes: The unantecedented "He" is correctly a `person` witness and both proper nouns carry their `Name` atoms. The clause-vs-VP boundary noted under q2 is what makes the missing connective atom arguable rather than certain.
